Rachel — thanks for the packet and the timeline. Attached are our initial responses and a companion exposure matrix that maps Helix's ask to our standard position plus the negotiable items. High-level callouts below; the completed questionnaire has inline explanations.

1) IP: Redwood does not require assignment of customer-derived IP. Customer retains rights to its data and outputs; we grant a limited, revocable service license necessary to provide the service. We flag one scenario (custom model training on customer data) where further terms are needed.

2) Indemnity: Redwood provides indemnity for third-party claims of IP infringement limited to claims arising from Redwood-delivered software and model code. We offer to defend and indemnify subject to customary notice and cooperation obligations. We cannot accept broad third-party claims arising from customer data misuse.

3) Liability cap: Our standard cap is the greater of $5,000,000 or 12 months of fees paid under the applicable order. For enterprise customers we can discuss higher caps tied to committed spend and SLAs. For certain high-sensitivity data use cases (PHI, regulated), we have tailored programs available under Redwood Private.

4) Data & Security: We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and can support on-site/remote audit requests per our SOC scope. Retention, logging, and audit evidence are captured in the attached exposure matrix.

Next steps: I've attached "Redwood_ExposureMatrix.xlsx" and a draft order form. Legal redlines to the order form or questionnaire are welcome at legal@redwood.com — we'll route to our counsel and get back with marked-up language within 3 business days for standard requests. For structural changes (e.g., cap uplift or indemnity expansion) I'll loop in our AEs.

Attachments: Redwood_ExposureMatrix.xlsx; Draft_OrderForm_Redwood.pdf

Happy to set a 30-minute sync this week to walk through the items.

Best,

Mina — appreciate the quick turnaround and the exposure matrix. A few clarifying questions for your legal team before we proceed to redlines:

• Data-exfiltration / cyber liabilities: Will Redwood accept carve-outs to the indemnity for breaches caused by Redwood security failures, and can you confirm whether compulsory cyber liability insurance limits are available?

• Open-source / model components: Our legal team needs confirmation that any third-party OSS or model components used in the delivered service are licensed appropriately and that Redwood will provide a list of such components upon request.

• SOC 2 / evidence: Can you commit to providing SOC2 Type II report within 10 business days of our formal request and indicate whether you support on-demand auditor access (remote)?

• Order form: We have a couple of non-substantive formatting asks, but two substantive items: we propose changing the liability cap to 24 months of fees (instead of 12) and adding an indemnity carve-out for regulatory fines arising from customer misuse. Please flag which of these are non-starters for Redwood.

Procurement is standing by for your answers; if helpful, we can set a short call to work through the liability matrix.

Thanks,

Hi Aisha / Rachel — thanks for the questions. Short answers and proposed path forward below.

• Cyber indemnity: Redwood will accept indemnity for direct losses caused by Redwood's failure to maintain reasonable security practices. We carry cyber insurance; certificate and limits available on request. We will not accept open-ended regulatory fine indemnities that arise solely from customer misuse.

• OSS / model components: We track third-party components as part of our model onboarding process. We can provide a component inventory and confirm license compliance; for proprietary model variants we will provide licensing summaries rather than source bundles.

• SOC2 access: We can provide SOC2 Type II attestation within 7 business days of request and support remote auditor access within the scope of our SOC engagement; on-site audits require advance notice and a separate SOW.

• Liability cap & order form: Our standard cap (greater of $5,000,000 or 12 months fees) is a foundational limit for hosted offerings. We can consider 24-month caps for a committed spend tier or as part of a Dedicated/Private deployment SOW. For now, we propose a compromise: interim negotiation language that ties any uplift to a minimum annual committed spend and SLA credits.

Next steps:
- I'll calendar a 30-min call with Rachel, Aisha, and our legal lead to review the exposure matrix.
- Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate commercial terms and draft a variant order form for your review.
- I'll upload our SOC2 report and the redline-ready order form to the Drive link and email procurement when ready.
